newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crudes limited to Gulf, arb tight.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crudes limited to Gulf, arb tight.

text.p: U.S. foreign crudes were limited into the U.S. Gulf and Atlantic coasts due to a tight arbitrage, but increasing lower Dated Brent levels were seen tempting sellers to move cargoes west, traders said.

The West Texas Intermediate/Brent arbitrage for October fell to $1.09 a barrel late Thursday, off another 10-15 cents from earlier this week, shutting import opportunities into the Gulf Coast, where stocks last week fell 5.5 million barrels.
Some traders said the import window was "semi-open", but the consensus was that Gulf refiners had little incentive to run incremental foreign barrels.
"I don't see a real buying push. The extra barrels are not getting run," an East Coast trader said.
A European major was seen fixing 600,000 barrels to the U.S. Gulf on a ship doing a return voyage, loading around September 13-15, but Brent barrels were not on offer.
Brent was notionally quoted at WTI parity to a few cents lower on a delivered basis, for Oct 1-10 arrival.

But traders said the fall in Dated Brent to Oct Brent minus 30-35 cents today may make Brent more competitive again, into the U.S., or act to pressure prices for substitute domestic grades such as Light Louisiana Sweet/St James.
But demand was noted for regional light, sweets such as Cusiana, with sellers showing second-half October barrels at Nov WTI parity fob.
Late Thursday, results were still pending for Ecopetrol's three-month Oct-Dec Cano Limon tender and Oct spot sale of Vasconia, traders said.
In the aftermarket, Brent intermonth Oct/Nov traded at 75 and 77 cents, about four cents higher than previously.
Oct Brent outright was pegged around $23.95 in late U.S. trade, with participants sidelined monitoring U.N.-Iraq tensions coming to a boil and bullish afterhours ACCESS.
